title: microsoft/vidur high-fidelity LLM inference simulator architecture and scheduling study
observations: Vidur is an MLSys'24 discrete-event LLM inference system simulator modeling execution time, continuous batching, and multi-node cluster topologies.

ExecutionTime explicitly decomposes pipeline-stage latency into projection kernels, attention (prefill chunk, decode, RoPE, KV save), MLP, collective communication (AllReduce vs Send/Recv), and host CPU scheduling/sampling/IPC overheads.
SklearnExecutionTimePredictor fits random forest and linear regressors over empirical operator execution profiling tables (Kineto/CUDA timers), caching models with cross-process locking.
Canary branch introduces prefix caching with hierarchical KV cache management (VRAM ReplicaKVCacheManager and host DiskKVCacheManager) and multi-replica global routing.
TolerantStickyLOPUncachedGlobalScheduler enforces conversational session affinity while preventing hot-spot stragglers via a tolerance-factor load imbalance slack window.
LOPUncachedGlobalScheduler routes requests based on remaining uncached prefill token volume rather than coarse request counts or binary cache hits.
CapacitySearch executes an adaptive binary search across QPS to determine maximum sustainable throughput within tail latency SLO bounds.
EDFRequestQueue schedules requests ordered by absolute deadline expiration rather than static integer priority.

candidates.effect: Slack-tolerant sticky session routing for cross-replica prefix cache locality without hot-spot stragglers.
candidates.outcome: Filed #10852 to add tolerance-factor slack window to FleetCacheRouter for multi-turn session load balancing.

candidates.effect: Route multi-replica requests by uncached prefill token volume rather than binary cache hits or request counts.
candidates.outcome: Filed #10853 to calculate uncached prefill tokens per replica and route to minimize peak pending token volume.

candidates.effect: Adaptive binary search for maximum sustainable throughput under strict latency SLOs.
candidates.outcome: Filed #10854 to add adaptive binary search over QPS discovering certified max throughput under latency SLOs.

candidates.effect: Earliest Deadline First (EDF) request queue for mixed interactive and batch latency SLO enforcement.
candidates.outcome: Filed #10856 to add deadline-ordered queuing to admission policy for mixed interactive/batch workloads.

candidates.effect: Decompose step latency into kernel projections and host CPU scheduling overheads in native performance profiling.
candidates.outcome: Filed #10861 to isolate GPU projection kernels from host CPU scheduling/sampling overheads in ProfileBundle.
